描述_EN: ding wares were often fired upside down, a strategy that served to spread the weight of the object onto the rim, guarding against any malformation of their thinly potted bodies during the firing. ding ware was a highly sought-after style of porcelain made in the ding kilns of the hebei province, that reached their height of popularity during the northern song (960-1127) and jin (1115-1234) dynasties. ding wares were of the earliest true porcelains made in china, and were known for their bright white bodies, impermeability and fine texture. while it displays the ding ware characteristics of a white colour and a decorative metal rim, its firing method reveals it as an imitation. they were produced as ‘official wares’ for use at court, and were highly esteemed throughout china. this dish was fired by a different method, evident from the spur marks at its centre (small imprints from the stand it rested on in the kiln), revealing it as an imitation of ding ware. this left behind an unglazed area at the rim, which was often hidden by a metal covering. this naturally resulted in the production of many imitations, including this dish (front left of image) from the haozhou kilns in the shanxi province.
描述_ZN: 鼎器通常是倒着烧的，这种策略是为了将器物的重量分散到边缘上，防止其薄薄的壶身在烧制过程中出现任何畸形。 定窑是河北省定窑制造的一种非常受欢迎的瓷器风格，在北宋（960-1127）和金（1115-1234）时期达到了鼎盛。 定窑是中国最早的真正意义上的瓷器，以其亮白的瓷体、不透水和精细的质地而闻名。 虽然它显示了白色和金属边缘装饰的鼎器特征，但它的烧制方法显示了它是一个仿制品。 它们是作为宫廷用的 "官器 "而生产的，在中国各地受到高度尊重。 这个盘子是用不同的方法烧制的，从它中心的刺痕（它在窑里的支架上留下的小印记）可以看出，它是一个仿丁器的产品。 这在边缘留下了一个未上釉的区域，它通常被一个金属罩子所隐藏。 这自然导致了许多仿制品的产生，包括这个来自山西省濠州窑的盘子（图片左前方）。
